statement: EMIB is characterised as better suited to ASICs than to high-bandwidth GPUs because of limited bridge area and routing density, even as its scaling is projected to improve.
why: If the alternative packaging route cannot serve the highest-bandwidth accelerators, relief from the packaging bottleneck reaches custom ASIC programs but not merchant GPUs.

impact.mechanism: Technical limits confine EMIB relief to ASIC workloads, so merchant-GPU packaging remains dependent on TSMC CoWoS while hyperscaler ASICs gain a second path.

evidence.source: TechSoda 'Global Market Watch: Advanced Packaging Takes the Stage' (Substack)
evidence.excerpt: but EMIB has 'limited bridge area and routing density' making it 'more suitable for ASICs than high-bandwidth, ultra-low-latency GPUs'

confidence.basis: Attributed to TrendForce analysis relayed in a secondary post; consistent with the stated technical description but not a primary engineering disclosure.
